reviews.title: Permanently banned for “falsified documents” and refused any explanation
reviews.text:
Upwork permanently deactivated my account after I uploaded my genuine, government-issued Spanish national ID to update my location after moving to Madrid. The email accused me of submitting “falsified or altered” documents and called it a “zero-tolerance” violation. I did nothing of the sort.

I immediately sent photos of both my Spanish and Dominican IDs and offered a live video call to verify myself. I got robotic, copy-pasted replies saying the decision is “final,” and that they are “unlikely to respond” to further messages. When I asked simply for an explanation of what supposedly was falsified, I was ignored. Not one agent explained what was flagged or looked at my evidence. To say their support agents were bad would be an understatement.

It gets worse: a separate automated reply to my appeal then claimed my account was “not found or active without any suspension” while their own emails confirmed it was blocked. Their systems and support don’t even agree with each other.

This is how a platform treats the freelancers whose work it profits from: accuse, ban, refuse to explain, and shut the door. No human review, no transparency, no real appeals process. If an automated check can wipe out your income and ruin your profile and records with no proof and no recourse, you are one flag away from losing everything. Avoid.

reviews.title: Upwork Needs to Treat Its Paying Clients Better.
reviews.text:
I’m a business owner who uses Upwork to hire professionals. My biggest concern isn’t the money. It’s how clients are treated when something goes wrong.

I hired a freelancer for a clearly defined project, provided original files and detailed instructions, and gave multiple opportunities to correct the work. Unfortunately, the freelancer couldn’t deliver what was agreed upon.

Upwork approved my $75 refund, which I appreciate. However, they described it as a “one-time courtesy.” That language was disappointing and left me questioning how future legitimate disputes would be handled.

Clients shouldn’t feel like they’re being done a favor when seeking a fair resolution for work that wasn’t delivered as agreed.

Upwork also needs better freelancer qualification standards and easier access to customer support.

I’ve worked with talented freelancers on this platform, and I want to continue using it. But Upwork needs to remember that business owners invest their money, time, and trust in its services.

It’s not about $75. It’s about accountability, respect, and treating customers fairly.

I submitted my proof through all the files and showed all of the evidence. Upward said they do not evaluate the quality of the completeness of the work, yet they recommended. I only received $56 for the completed work while refunding the client $168. After declining that settlement, the next step was arbitration costing $337 per party. More than the entire milestone being. It makes it economically unfeasible to pursue small contracts, especially when it leans heavily towards the client versus protect protecting the free worked on. I’ve simply lost full confidence in the app and their ability to protect their users I would highly recommend those considering two use the app, to reconsider.

reviews.title: Account Permanently Suspended Due to Verification Error- No Human Support
reviews.text:
My Upwork account was permanently suspended after a verification issue that I never received an explanation for. I followed every instruction the site gave, and waited- only to be told my account was closed with no meaningful details about what went wrong. 
When I tried to resolve this I could not reach a human. The only option was a chat bot, which repeated the same response over and over again and never escalated my case. I repeatedly typed requests to speak with an agent and to escalate to Trust and Safety, but the bot kept sending generic  troubleshooting steps and links that led nowhere. After days of back-and-forth with automated system I still have access to my account, no clear reason for the suspension, and no human review.
This response cost me time, income and trust. Upwork’s verification process and customer support are broken: automated systems are allowed to make permanent account decisions without any real oversight or a reliable appeals path. If you value fair review and the ability to speak to a real person about account issues, DO NOT RELY ON UPWORK.

reviews.title: All crashing
reviews.text:
Great platform, but a very frustrating experience overall. The app keeps crashing and getting stuck every time I try to use it. I paid $29 to boost a job posting, but I was charged twice. I’ve been trying to figure out how to correct the duplicate charge, but the app makes it very difficult to get support or resolve the issue.

On top of that, trying to log in is another headache. It keeps asking security questions — honestly, who remembers security answers today after logging in from so many devices . The platform should offer easier and more easier verification options, like text message or email verification codes, to make the login process smoother and more user-friendly.

reviews.title: Filled with Scams
reviews.text: Really disappointed with my experience. I’ve heard good things, but I’ve only had a negative experience. Most of the jobs I’ve applied to have been scams. I appreciate that they refund me the credits when the job is taken down. But for a service that is paid, I’d expect there to be a better system in place to make sure these are legitimate jobs before freelancers can apply. On top of it all, I can tell someone stole my data because i have been receiving nonstop spam calls every day now since I joined UpWork, yet zero interviews or anyone contacting me through the app. It’s so disappointing that it’s nearly impossible to apply for jobs now anywhere without my information getting leaked.

reviews.title: A broken "Pay-to-Play" system that favors scammers over professionals.
reviews.text:
Upwork has officially transitioned from a professional marketplace to a high-stakes gambling site where the Upwork always wins but you lose. The platform is now overrun with sophisticated scams, identity theft attempts, and AI voice-harvesting schemes.

The 'Connects' system is predatory; you are forced to pay a premium just to apply for jobs that, more often than not, are phishing attempts. I’ve encountered several 'Verified' clients misrepresenting legitimate companies only to lure freelancers into external Google Forms or Drive requests to steal data and intellectual property.

Upwork’s security is non-existent. They profit from every bid we place on these fake listings but offer zero accountability or human support when a report is filed. It’s a massive asymmetric power dynamic where the freelancer takes all the financial and security risks while the company collects fees from both sides. Unless you want to pay for the 'privilege' of being scammed, stay away.

reviews.title: High stress platform
reviews.text: A lot to unpack about this platform. Although many find it useful but it will drain you to build up, and will drain your budget to keep applying for gigs. Applying is not free and you've only got a number of connects to spend before you have to keep spending on buying connects in hopes of getting hired. This is not a good strategy for any entrepreneur that is just starting. And my only other option is to buy their premium service for more connects and insights. But in this saturated market, this makes it very frustrating and almost impossible to kick off without spending a respectable amount of money in hopes of one job. And you spend with absolutely no guarantees that you will get anything, even with a polished profile. So in my opinion it is EXTREMELY monetized.

reviews.title: Predatory and Essentially a Slot Machine
reviews.text: The app itself as well designed although every five seconds seems to be checking if I’m a robot or not, which is pretty obnoxious. My big gripe is that, concerning software development, both the clientele that post jobs and the worldwide reach make it a highly competitive and unsustainable platform to take part in. Why pay a highly qualified western resident their rate if someone in Asia does it for a nickel? And not only does upwork charge you for a subscription, they then charge you that nonsense token fee for the privilege of bidding on the chance to offer your services, and, then, of course, they also take a giant chunk out of your earnings. Just a predatory business that I won’t revisit.
